     P.O Box 390                  GIRDWOOD VALLEY SERVICE AREA BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
      Girdwood, Alaska 99587                               Jennifer Wingard & Kellie Okonek, Co-Chairs
      http://www.muni.org/gbos                             Brian Burnett, Amanda Tuttle, Nick Crews
    Suzanne LaFrance, Mayor
                                 July 30 2026
                    GBOS Budget Meeting #2
                              Minutes Final
        10:00 a.m. via Microsoft Teams & Girdwood Community Room

This hybrid meeting is taking place via Microsoft Teams & at the Girdwood Community Room, 250 Egloff Rd:


The Girdwood Board of Supervisors is subject to the Alaska Open Meetings Act as found in Alaska Statute 44.62.310
and Anchorage Municipal Code1.25 - Public Meetings.
The Girdwood Board of Supervisors operates under the Girdwood Public Meetings Standards of Conduct.

Call to Order 10:00 a.m. Brian Burnett

Land Acknowledgement: The Girdwood Board of Supervisors acknowledges the indigenous peoples of Alaska, whose land we
reside on. The community of Girdwood, situated between the areas known to be Dena'ina and Alutiiq homeland, respects the people
who were stewards of this land for generations. We commit to the continued stewardship of this land and are grateful to be part of a
wider community that seeks to maintain a sustainable use of Girdwood Valley for present and future peoples.

Roll Call: Brian Burnett (BB), Amanda Tuttle (AT), Nick Crews (NC)
Jennifer Wingard and Kellie Okonek are excused.
No Disclosures

Agenda Revisions and Approval:    July 30 2026 GBOS meeting agenda approved AT/NC

Agenda:
1.     Review of 2027 proposed budgets
Overview of budget/mill rate and how Girdwood compares to other tax districts in MOA.
Current budget proposed is a 3.86% increase, total cost of $226,744 over last year’s budge.

720 single family parcels, 65 of them have ADU
512 condos, 102 duplex/triplex/fourplex
Total approx. 2000 parcels with buildings
Nick Crews provided analysis of the tax in Girdwood, which will be added to the meeting packet.

Staff will research how many new building permits have been issued in the last 3 years.

Fire Department Budget
Increase in labor, Operating, uniforms, insurance
IGC’s went down in 2026 1Q revisions after request for review of them. Chief still has questions, as well as on other
IGC’s, such has Ombudsman and GIS mapping. She has a meeting coming up to review IGCs and will request some
relief from these fees, as discussed at the MOA GBOS meeting on Monday.

           GBOS Meeting Agendas and minutes are available on line: http://www.muni.org/gbos

                                                                                         1

Housing and Economic Stability Budget
2026 budget had $100,000 for housing study, which is not yet spent and RFP not yet on the street, due to other
purchasing priorities of the GVSA.
2027 budget has $100,000 for anticipated RV Park feasibility study. This item is considered for other funding options
(TIPS).
GBOS requests staff add to GBOS agenda, assessment of what kinds of things can GHEC spend funds on.

Roads Budget
Increase in labor, roads contract re-bid (due now, but stuck in purchasing currently)


Parks and Recreation Budget
Increase in labor
Review of IGC’s includes building maintenance, Little Bears and Glacier City Hall maintenance is funded through this.
GBOS requests staff add Little Bears Building to future agenda.

Group discusses non-profit grant structure and hard-funding for Glacier Valley Transit. Possible consideration to add
this to TIPS ideas, move to funding via GHEC budget item if it fits there better than as a recreation item, or increase
the hard funding via grant. GBOS doesn’t have much information on GVT budget or funding.

GBOS requests that director of GVT attend a future meeting to review this so that they understand better the
challenges facing the non-profit. Amanda Tuttle will reach out to GVT director regarding this.

Police Budget
Flat Budget, last year in this contract without increase.


Unspent funds drop to the Girdwood Undesignated fund and can be used for other GVSA projects, as directed by the
GBOS and approved by the Assembly.

GBOS members may submit proposed budget changes to Kyle via email or bring them to budget meeting #3 for
consideration prior to budget review and vote in September. Amendments may be made by motion at the final
meeting.

2.      Capital Projects Budgets
Reviewed prioritized list of projects for the GVSA
Staff will add capital and undesignated funds to present at the 3rd budget meeting.


3.    MOA Budget requests: TIPS and Public Safety funds
TIPS Ideas:
RV Park Study
Public restrooms
Glacier Valley Transit funding
GHEC and others will also make recommendations
GBOS should select priority item(s) to forward to MOA at their August meeting.

Public Safety Funds Ideas:
Not discussed, need to be Public Safety IT items used within the MOA only (not shared with Whittier service).

4.     Consider Budget Meeting 3 week of August 24
        Staff will poll  for Aug 27-31 for meeting #3
       Set date for GVSA non-profit grant presentations after Sept GBOS meeting
        Staff will poll for dates after Sept 21.


Public Comment:    None
Adjourn 12PM
